Manufacturing applications should foreground process capability, setup, repeatability, inspection, waste, and safe production. A laser-cut template can support machining or assembly, but it is not automatically a precision instrument or a load-rated machine component.

## Project directions

:::: {.ter-project-grid}
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Setup-block and datum kit
<p class="ter-course-code">TMJ2O / senior TMJ · Gauge family</p>
Create a labelled set of reference blocks for rapid layout, then verify each finished dimension against a trusted instrument.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Drawing → process plan → trial coupon → fabricate → inspect → record deviation</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Datums, tolerances, caliper use, inspection record, non-conformance</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · 10–50 mm reference blocks</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Stable sheet or machined stock appropriate to the intended accuracy</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Protect datum edges; add a case that prevents mixing pieces</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Shop reference only unless calibrated through an approved process</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=manufacturing&type=jigs-gauges">Manufacturing gauges</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/03-measure-place.qmd">Measure + Place</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Create an inspection report with nominal, actual, error, and disposition</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Visual tool-control board
<p class="ter-course-code">TMJ2O · Organizer family</p>
Design a shadow-board module for one real tool set so missing tools and incorrect placement are obvious at a glance.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Inventory → trace/measure → placement study → prototype retention → load test</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>5S thinking, reach, tool clearance, labelling, assembly planning</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · one bounded module, not a whole shop wall</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Plywood face with suitable retainers and verified mounting system</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Backer and fasteners carry load; thin decorative parts do not</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Heavy or sharp tools require positive retention and instructor approval</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=manufacturing&type=tool-holders">Manufacturing holder kits</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/07-wall-bench-module.qmd">Wall + Bench Module</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Time retrieval and return before and after the redesign</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Repeatable assembly fixture
<p class="ter-course-code">Senior TMJ · Portable work module</p>
Build a low-force fixture that locates parts consistently during marking or a classroom assembly operation.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Task analysis → 3-2-1 locating concept → prototype → capability trial</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Workholding, constraints, poka-yoke, cycle observation, revision</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Advanced · bench fixture under 400 mm</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Plywood/acrylic prototype; metal only when process and equipment justify it</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Separate locators from clamps; state forces and wear points</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Never use an unreviewed fixture in powered cutting or high-force operations</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=manufacturing&type=core-geometry">Exact geometry starters</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../01-nice-design-process/04-prototype-evaluate-iterate.qmd">Prototype, Evaluate & Iterate</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Run ten samples and report variation, failure modes, and redesign</dd></dl>
:::
